messages:
alexh: quick sync — we need to nail down ownership and scope for the onboarding metrics that feed admit/compat checks. Currently it's unclear who owns 'compat_coverage' vs 'smoke_pass_rate'. Thoughts? :thinking:

maria_g: +1. My take: infra owns collection/ETL and metric plumbing, ML owns signal definitions, threshold semantics, and alerting logic. If ownership is mixed we get slow triage.

jin: agree. Also we should separate 'golden_sample_coverage' from 'compat_coverage' — golden is about canonical inputs coverage, compat is about runtime-compat signals (tokenizer, logits shape, runtime errors).

samir: ops note — we need a canonical namespace and tag strategy. propose `onboard.acceptance_rate`, `onboard.smoke_pass_rate`, `onboard.golden_coverage`, `onboard.latency_p50`, `onboard.latency_p95`. Tags: `bench_v`, `model_hash`, `env` (canary/prod).

leah: +1 to tags. Also ownership for bench_v itself: who updates bench_v when we change inputs or postprocess? We should treat bench_v like infra schema and require changelog. Otherwise acceptance_rate drifts for no reason.

maria_g: can we get the console to show bench_v as a dimension? that would make triage so much faster. also we should add an `eval_regression` alert: triggers when quality drop > 3% on golden set across bench_v stable window.

alexh: actionable summary: 1) ML to write a short signal semantics doc (names + precise defs) 2) Infra to implement metric exports + tagging (bench_v, model_hash, env) 3) Product to add deck panels for bench_v + model filters. target: sync next week. @maria_g @jin please ack.

onboard-bot: created ticket #INF-4832 'onboard-metrics-ownership' assigned to @maria_g, due 2024-06-12

jin: one more architectural tradeoff: do we block models pre-admit on hard thresholds or allow admit + automatic rollback by monitoring? Pre-admit is safer but expensive (full bench runs). Post-admit rollback is faster to iterate but risks customer impact.

samir: cost perspective: full deep bench for every submission multiplies infra spend. hybrid approach: pre-admit lightweight smoke + targeted deep-bench on canary traffic or on-demand. also consider sampling rare long sequences rather than full dataset every time.

leah: snippet for metric sample (for infra):
```
{
  "metric": "onboard.golden_coverage",
  "value": 0.92,
  "tags": {"bench_v":"v2.1", "model":"gpt-3a", "env":"canary"}
}
```

alexh: thanks y'all. i'll consolidate into the RFC follow-up doc and add the owners to INF-4832. if nobody objects i'll mark ML owner = `maria_g` for signal defs and Infra owner = `samir` for export/tags. :thumbsup:
